lines.en: label shrine40:
scene noonsky
There is naught to do in summer but bathe in the muggy omnipotence of its tangible, suffocating humidity- so thick that I can feel it embracing me as I make my way up a familiar set of stairs.
I can see distorted lines in the air from where it has gotten confused, and I do my best to look past them as making them even more self-conscious would not bode well for the weather.

If you’re wondering what I’m talking about, you’re not alone. For thoughts like these have been plaguing me for thirty minutes as I’ve become fed up with this mid-year glow and all it means for Kumon-mi.
Soon enough, the cold will return — and with it will come the death of something that never should have been in the first place.
The sun, and all its toxic rays.
scene black
The distorted shape of summer tapers off along with the last of the stairs as something else comes into my line of sight.
scene mayanemaiden1
Can you see it too?
Or does the appearance of something you’re unable to explain hurt you more than any amount of the heat’s embrace ever could?
: Is something wrong, Maya?
: Something is always wrong.
: It’s hot, this dress is heavier than it looks, and to complicate things even more, you’re here now.
: I can leave if you want.
: Okay. See you.
: Actually, I think I’ll stay.
: It’s extremely irritating how your existence continues to...irritate me even after the most...irritating parts of it have gone away.
: I’m starting to think you might be irritated.
: Shut up. It’s hot.
It’s funny to think of how little things have changed after all we’ve been through.
In fact, I feel like most of my early conversations here were just like this.
I’d show up out of nowhere, seek out a young girl a full foot shorter than me, and then promptly ruin her day because something about annoying her made me feel a little more human.
Just being around her now has that effect.
And even when she looks at me like that, in complete disregard for all the two of us have gone through-
I want nothing more than to remove her dress, carry her back to my room, and make her cry out my name.
My real name.
: Can you save your disgusting, lustful glares for when I am not melting? Thanks.
: My room has air conditioning, you know.
scene mayanemaiden2
: Okay, so I guess that’s a “no.” Wonderful.
: Wonderful indeed. So, are you ready to talk about that thing I said to you on the beach? Or are we really going to keep ignoring it?
: Now is...really not the time for that.
: Any reason why? Or are you just continuing to avoid me because it makes things more convenient and-
: Sensei!
scene mayanemaiden3
: Oh, okay. I get it now.
: Just kill me already. I’m starting to miss the more peaceful cycles from before I had feelings and bonds I had to worry about.
: Thanks for having tons of sex with me the other day! I had a great time!
: And that. That might be the worst part of all.
: Ayane, let’s not talk about what we do in our free time around...literally anyone else. Let alone at a- wait, why are you also a shrine maiden all of a sudden?
scene mayanemaiden4
: Because she’s starting to become just as obsessed with me as she is with you. Thanks for that.
: How is that my fault? Ayane got attached to you on her own and I had nothing to do with it.
: You had a little bit to do with it.
: You’re not helping. And that still doesn’t explain where you got the dress or why you’re here instead of the dojo.
: I gave her the dress, obviously.
: Well, no wonder she’s obsessed with you. You’re giving her free stuff. Be more like me if you want her to go away. I never give her anything.
: That’s not true. You give me that dick all the time.
scene mayanemaiden5
: Didn’t I ask you to sweep the inside of the shrine?
: I finished up as quickly as I could when I heard Sensei’s footsteps coming up the stairs.
: Well...go do it again. It’s distracting having to listen to you brag about your sex life all day now that you’re no longer practicing abstinence.
: Can someone please explain to me why Ayane is a shrine maiden now or are we going to keep annoying Maya instead?
: I’m fine with the latter, I just don’t know what level of seriousness we’re going for today.
scene mayanemaiden6
: Hah...
: The reason I gave her the dress and the reason I’m having her tidy up the shrine is because it seemed like the most...practical option considering her newfound interest in my daily routine.
: I figured that if she’s going to be hanging around here, I should at least have her work so our time is not entirely wasted.
: Me working here means that we get to talk about more reset-stuff too.
: And since nobody else ever really shows up, we don’t have to worry about some other girl from class appearing at the wrong time and thinking we’re plotting a takeover of the universe or something.
: I think there’s a higher likelihood that someone like that would just interrupt us, but I suppose that’s not really important right now.
scene mayanemaiden7
: At the end of the day, I see minimal harm in taking on an apprentice if that apprentice is going to actually work. Plus, having someone to brainstorm with is also a bit of a bonus.
: We can chalk Ayane’s new role up to just...formal inclusion and proof of her new place in this never-ending timeline.
: Phase one, rooftop apocalypse buddy! Phase two, coworker-slash-shrine maiden buddy!
: What’s phase three?
scene mayanemaiden8
: A bride!
: Did you really have to ask?
: Mine? Or Maya’s? Because the other two phases both involved her.
scene mayanemaiden9
: I don’t like girls. But Maya is cute and I’d probably marry her for tax purposes if I make it to twenty and Sensei still doesn’t-
: Rejected.
: Oh well. My family’s rich and I probably won’t even have to pay taxes anyway. But if you change your mind and-
: No.
: You tried, Ayane. And that’s all you can really do with Maya.
: I’ll get her to love me one day. I can feel it.
: So, is this just...what you two do now? Hang out at a shrine and talk about time travel?
: That’s not much different from what I usually do. The only substantial change is that I now have to hear about how great you are every five minutes.
: I’m sure I’ll work up an immunity to it sooner or later like I have with basically everything else.
: Hey, if getting involved in the resets is all it took to land me a job here, does that mean everyone else gets to become a shrine maiden too if they all wind up making it to the roof?
: This is a question I take personal interest in, so I’d like to hear an answer to this as well.
scene mayanemaiden10
: Ayane, please don’t forget that this whole thing with you is some strange fluke and that the likelihood of anyone else getting roped into this reset business is basically zero.
: Right, yeah. Because you haven’t gotten any other prediction wrong so far. I forgot about that.
: Please don’t make me regret the decision to let you get closer to me in sheer physical proximity only with zero room for substantial emotional attachment.
: Aww, I love you too.
: What if someone else does make it up there, though?
scene mayanemaiden11
: Are you only asking because you want to see them in the dress as well?
: No. I’m asking for the sake of the universe. But the dress part does help.
scene noonsky
: Ugh...I guess that’s just one more bridge we’ll have to figure out how to cross if we ever manage to make it there.
: For now, I think it would be best if we were to come up with some sort of gameplan on what we want to accomplish this cycle.
: During the last one, we discovered that it is not entirely impossible for others to gain some sort of awareness as well. Which would mean that this time-
: We need to test that theory again, right?
scene mayanemaiden12
: Uhh...yes, actually. But how did you know I was going to say that?
: Because I’ve been secretly traveling through time longer than you and know everything that is going to happen from this point onward.
: Spoiler alert, I end up with Sensei.
: Sure, but how did you actually-
: Because it’s the same thing you did last time with the whole pregnancy thing.
: You came up with a theory and decided to spend the entirety of the last cycle testing that theory and inflicting a great deal of suffering on both Sensei and me.
: It’s not really science if things happen only one time, so experiments like this are good for when you want to prove that something wasn’t just a fluke.
: Which is, surprisingly enough, a thing you directly contradicted by calling me a fluke a few minutes ago.
: But hey, if you want to only believe in certain things when they make you sound smarter then, by all means, proceed.
: You know, you spend so much time being absolutely unbearable that I forget how smart you really are sometimes.
: I know. I’m a real catch, aren’t I?
scene mayanemaiden13
: What Ayane said just now was right.
: The...part about her being a catch?
: Sensei already knows that. You don’t have to remind him.
: Not that part. The part about needing to test this theory of other girls catching onto the resets.

: It didn’t happen until very late in the cycle last time, so if we can manage to convince someone we’re not completely insane a little earlier this time, we might have better luck finding something out.
: Okay...but then what?
: Then...we know more things. It’s called learning. As a teacher, this information should be invaluable to you.
: What Maya means to say is that if we learn things quickly enough, you might get a third shrine maiden soon.
: That I can understand and it is something I will strive for. Thank you, Ayane.
: Don’t mention it.
: Can you maybe attempt having some sort of drive that doesn’t pertain to young girls in costumes in the future? Or is this just what I’ve signed up for?
: If anyone should know, I think it should be you.
: It is. I was just looking for a little false encouragement as it might make this terrible day slightly more bearable for a few minutes.
: Then I will do it for science.
scene mayanemaiden14
: Ugh, forget it. You’re a terrible liar and asking someone as self-serving and incompetent as you to do anything just makes me look like an idiot.
: Is there anyone you have in mind as a target? Should we try our luck with Yumi and Tsuneyo again? Maybe see if they have some...lingering memories from the last reset or something?
: I...attempted speaking with Tsuneyo on my own, but I think it’s safe to say she doesn’t remember anything. As far as Yumi goes...I’d rather not approach her.
: I can talk to Yumi. That would probably go a little better than either of you-
: What about Ami?
scene mayanemaiden15
: Ami?
: Yeah! She’s the closest to us out of everyone and I’m sure she’d be open to hearing us out. Especially since it’ll help her feel less excluded and stuff.
: She might think we’re a little crazy at first, but she’s gullible enough to start believing us if we keep pressing her about it.
: Ami’s not a good idea, Ayane.
scene mayanemaiden16
: She’s not? Why?
: It’s...a long and complicated story.
: I mean...I don’t have anything else going on. You can tell me about it if you want.
: I’m afraid the story is far too long and far too complicated to just tell you. I wouldn’t be recounting some tale of how I was banned from a convenience store or anything like that.
: I’d be describing probably decades or...centuries of trying that exact thing to no avail as I thought the same thing as you.
: And not only did it never work, it made her...mad.
: It’s just not worth the effort.
: Ami? Mad? But if it doesn’t involve Sensei, she basically never gets mad. And Sensei wasn’t a recurring thing for this until a couple cycles ago, right?
: Yes and...no. That’s also a little too complicated to just casually recount.
scene mayanemaiden17
: Well...we can sideline the Ami thing for now and maybe talk more about that later. I can tell by that face that this might be a touchy subject for you.
: Thank you. I think Yumi remains our strongest prospect for the moment, but I’m sure there are other names that might pop up as this iteration of the school year goes by.
scene mayanemaiden18
: What matters most is that we do something. Time itself might be infinite, but who knows if ours is?
: Understood?
: Yes, captain. Just tell me what to do and I’ll do it.
: Excellent. Go away.
scene noonsky
: Got it.
: Wha-
: Did that...actually work?
: Maya! You can’t just send our boyfriend away like that! He’s sensitive!
: Our what? Shouldn’t you be sweeping?
: Sensei! Wait for me! I’ll love you when she can’t!
Ayane chases after me as I go to leave, but is promptly grabbed by the collar as Maya drags her back under the protection of whatever god resides here.
I’m not leaving because I was told to, but I’m sure you probably understand that based on my history here.
It’s just far too disgusting out here today and...
And staring so long at something I can not have hurts me more than any amount of the heat’s embrace ever could.
scene black
This cycle will melt the wax of my wings.
I’m flying too close to the sun.
